items.followUp: Differentiate between a web browser and a web server.

rubric.why: Shows the basic role difference between a server and a client.
rubric.description: States that a server provides services or resources and a client requests them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both roles are correctly distinguished.

rubric.why: Explains what the client does with the server’s response.
rubric.description: States that the client uses the services or resources supplied by the server.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the client’s use of server resources.

modelAnswer: A server system provides services or resources to other computers on a network.
A client system requests and uses the services or resources provided by a server.

items.followUp: Write the names of two attributes of the <a> tag.

rubric.why: src specifies the image file to display.
rubric.description: Names the src attribute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming src.

rubric.why: These are other valid attributes of the img tag.
rubric.description: Names another valid img attribute, such as alt, height or width.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming any one valid attribute other than src.

modelAnswer: Two attributes of the tag are src and alt.

items.followUp: Write the HTML code to make the word COMPUTER bold.

rubric.why: The i or em tag applies italic emphasis.
rubric.description: Uses a valid italic tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using <i> or <em>.

rubric.why: The requested word must be placed inside the italic tag.
rubric.description: Includes PAKISTAN as the content to be italicised.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including the correct word within the tag.

modelAnswer: PAKISTAN

items.followUp: Differentiate between software testing and debugging, giving an example of each.

rubric.why: Verification checks whether work is being done according to requirements or specifications.
rubric.description: Defines verification in relation to requirements or specifications.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition of verification.

rubric.why: Validation checks whether the completed product meets user needs or its intended use.
rubric.description: Defines validation in relation to user needs or intended use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition of validation.

rubric.why: A relevant example distinguishes checking work products against specifications.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of verification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant verification example.

rubric.why: A relevant example shows the product being checked against actual user needs.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of validation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant validation example.

modelAnswer: Verification checks whether the product is being developed according to specified requirements; it asks, “Are we building the product right?”
Example: reviewing a design or code to check that it follows the requirements.
Validation checks whether the completed product meets users’ needs; it asks, “Are we building the right product?”
Example: users test the completed software to see whether it performs the tasks they need.

items.followUp: Explain four advantages of using a computer network.

rubric.why: Networks allow connected users to share hardware devices.
rubric.description: Explains hardware or device sharing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining a network benefit related to sharing hardware.

rubric.why: Networks make it possible to share data, files or software.
rubric.description: Explains sharing of data, files or software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining a network benefit related to sharing information or software.

rubric.why: Networks support communication between users in different locations.
rubric.description: Explains communication as a network benefit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct communication benefit.

rubric.why: Sharing resources or managing information centrally can reduce costs and simplify management.
rubric.description: Explains a further benefit, such as reduced cost or centralised management.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly explained additional network benefit.

modelAnswer: A computer network allows users to share hardware, such as printers, instead of needing a separate device for each computer.
Users can share files, data and software over the network.
A network enables fast communication between users through services such as email or video conferencing.
Sharing resources and managing data centrally can reduce costs and make administration easier.

items.followUp: Explain any four ways people can protect themselves from cyber crime.

rubric.why: Hacking involves gaining unauthorised access to computer systems or data.
rubric.description: Explains hacking.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and correctly explaining hacking.

rubric.why: Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to steal sensitive information.
rubric.description: Explains phishing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and correctly explaining phishing.

rubric.why: Identity theft involves using another person’s personal information or identity fraudulently.
rubric.description: Explains identity theft.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and correctly explaining identity theft.

rubric.why: Software piracy and cyberbullying are both valid cyber crimes when correctly explained.
rubric.description: Explains another valid cyber crime, such as software piracy or cyberbullying.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and correctly explaining one further cyber crime.

modelAnswer: Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to a computer system or its data.
Phishing is using fake emails or websites to trick people into revealing passwords or other personal information.
Identity theft is using another person’s personal information to impersonate them or commit fraud.
Software piracy is illegally copying or distributing copyrighted software.

items.followUp: Explain the steps in the top-down design approach to solving a problem.

rubric.why: The strategy begins by breaking a large problem into manageable parts.
rubric.description: Explains that the problem is divided into smaller subproblems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the division step.

rubric.why: The smaller parts are solved and their results combined into a complete solution.
rubric.description: Explains solving the parts and combining their results.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the solve-and-combine steps.

modelAnswer: Divide a large problem into smaller, manageable subproblems.
Solve the subproblems and combine their results to produce the solution to the original problem.

items.followUp: Draw and label the flowchart symbols for input/output and decision.

rubric.why: An oval represents start/end and a rectangle represents a process.
rubric.description: Draws or identifies the terminal and process symbols.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly showing or naming both symbols.

rubric.why: A parallelogram represents input/output and a diamond represents a decision.
rubric.description: Draws or identifies the input/output and decision symbols.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly showing or naming both symbols.

modelAnswer: Terminal (Start/End): draw an oval.
Process: draw a rectangle.
Input/Output: draw a parallelogram.
Decision: draw a diamond.
